title: Quickstart scoped mode
claim: Push1 at main startup or alternate entry, pop at corresponding exit; CSI/u/tilde/letter families plus C0 exceptions.

title: CSI grammar
claim: 7-bit ESC [; decimal fields separated by semicolons, subfields by colons; mandatory key number; u terminator; optional remaining fields.

title: Unshifted key identity
claim: Primary codepoint represents unshifted key even with Shift; preserve Unicode scalar identity.

title: Shifted and base-layout alternatives
claim: Shifted identity occurs only with Shift; base-only requires empty shifted subfield; producer may lack either identity.

title: Modifier vocabulary
claim: Eight bits: Shift1 Alt2 Ctrl4 Super8 Hyper16 Meta32 Caps64 Num128; decimal parameter is mask+1, omitted means1; modifier-key event includes its resulting state.

title: Event kinds
claim: Press1 default; repeat2 and release3 only when requested; plain text cannot carry event kind without all-keys.

title: Associated Unicode text
claim: Colon-separated codepoints; pure text with unknown key uses0; no C0/C1 controls; do not reconstruct consumed OS modifiers.

title: Functional key population
claim: Functional table is authoritative, including special C0 identities and non-u finals; PUA range alone does not assign a key.

title: Replace/add/remove flags
claim: =flags;mode u: omitted mode1; modes1/2/3 replace/or/clear selected bits; all five bits independently queryable.

title: Query current flags
claim: ?u query yields ?flags u from terminal to requesting application; query is nonmutating.

title: Push/pop/bounds
claim: Push omitted flags0; pop omitted count1; separate screen stacks, pop empty resets flags, full push evicts oldest; exact limit unspecified.

title: Independent main and alternate stacks
claim: Changes in alternate stack must not affect main stack; physical stack representation is implementation detail.

title: Flag1
claim: Esc and listed ASCII modified keys disambiguate; distinguish nontext keypad; Enter/Tab/Backspace keep legacy exceptions; text locks need all-keys.

title: Flag2
claim: Repeat otherwise acts as press; release otherwise absent; Enter/Tab/Backspace release needs flag8 too.

title: Flag4
claim: Only enriches already escaped keys; cannot itself force plain text into escape sequences.

title: Flag8
claim: All keys escaped, modifier-key events included, raw text suppressed; implies disambiguation behavior without requiring bit1 in queried flags.

title: Flag16
claim: Adds text to all-key reports; without flag8 behavior explicitly undefined.

title: Support detection
claim: Query followed by primary DA; DA arriving without enhancement response means unsupported; set/query detects subset support; all enhancements strongly encouraged.

title: Default fallback
claim: Legacy default sends text UTF8, repeat indistinguishable from press; encodings outside legacy described forms use CSI-u, subject to explicit optional functional-key exception.

title: Legacy functional encodings
claim: Terminfo-specific CSI/SS3 forms, unmodified cursor-mode alternates; omit absent modifiers and lock bits.

title: Legacy C0 and keypad
claim: Use explicit C0 table; backspace inversion is terminfo-dependent; keypad keys collapse to non-keypad; unmapped functional emission may be disabled.

title: Legacy ASCII algorithm
claim: Alt prefixes ESC; Ctrl uses explicit mapping; else Shift then original; other modifier combinations use CSI-u; illustrative ambiguity prose is not a new mapping.

title: Every functional table entry
claim: Use every named key and every explicitly allowed representation; F3 uses13~ (CSI R removed due CPR conflict).

title: Every legacy Ctrl mapping
claim: Explicit mapping; unlisted ASCII remains unchanged, not unconditional bitmask.

title: Fixterms corrections
claim: Preserve directionality, Shift/base identity, Super, Esc and Ctrl+Shift+Tab corrections; conflicting illustrative claims require decision.

title: modifyOtherKeys discussion
claim: Rationale is not a new wire protocol. RMUX coexistence/precedence with modifyOtherKeys needs explicit policy.

title: Invalid, unknown and bounded recovery
claim: Pinned grammar constrains validity; recovery, size, timer, unknown-bit and unknown-key handling are RMUX policy, not specified conformance.

title: Fragmentation/coalescence
claim: Transport boundaries must not alter a complete logical event or reply; bound retained fragments and preserve other terminal control families.

title: Client/pane ownership and consumption
claim: Binding, copy, mode-tree, popup and application routes share one normalized event; captured press ownership controls repeat/release; no unavailable metadata invented.

title: Reset/replacement/attach lifetime
claim: RIS/DECSTR, alt reentry, child exit/respawn, detach/suspend/lock/reconnect and stale identities need separate product decisions and native evidence.

title: Native and public input fidelity
claim: Unix bytes, Windows records/VT, Web tokens/text/raw bytes, SDK and Ratatui host inputs expose distinct metadata; unknown input metadata stays unknown.

title: Outer negotiation/restoration
claim: Outer handshake and restoration belong to client attachment generation, separate from pane stacks; no untagged stale reply may mutate new ownership.
